passages.original: tum naturae necessitas cogebat, uere fatebor, non si ipse, ut aiunt, ab inferis Homerus emergeret, posset exponere: adeo omnia maiora in Martino sunt, quam ut uerbis concipi queant. numquam hora ulla momentumque praeteriit, quo non aut orationi incumberet aut insisteret lectioni, quamquam etiam inter legendum aut si quid aliud forte agebat, numquam animum ab oratione laxabat.
passages.english: [...] then the necessity of nature compelled [him], I will truly confess, not even if Homer himself, as they say, were to rise from the dead could he set it forth: so much greater are all things in Martin than can be grasped in words. Never did any hour or moment pass in which he was not either intent on prayer or devoted to reading, although even in the midst of reading, or if he happened to be doing anything else, he never relaxed his mind from prayer.
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence; the opening clause ('tum naturae necessitas cogebat', 'then the necessity of nature compelled [him]') depends on preceding text not supplied, probably a clause such as 'except when' (nisi cum) referring to the times Martin took food or sleep.
